title: Hardware & Power

panels.title: GPUs visible
panels.description: nvidia_gpu_count from the gpu-exporter. Red when below app_settings prometheus.threshold.expected_gpu_count. NVIDIA device nodes bind at container-CREATE time, so a card the exporter container was created without is invisible with no error and a plain restart will NOT fix it — recreate the container. An RTX 3090 was missing here for 7+ days (2026-07-26) while still drawing ~42W.

panels.title: Gaming
panels.description: Pipeline pauses automatically when external GPU workload (gaming) is detected

panels.title: Detected VRAM pool
panels.description: Total GPU VRAM across all cards (sum of nvidia_gpu_memory_total_mib). This is the number the dispatcher's gpu_vram_total_gb="auto" budget guard derives.

panels.title: Render VRAM gate — free (render GPU)
panels.description: Free VRAM on the render/display GPU (pipeline_gpu_index=0, the 5090) right now. Below media_render_min_free_vram_gb (default 25 GB → red) the media dispatch gate DEFERS video renders so a ~24 GB Wan render can't oversubscribe the card and spill WDDM into system RAM (the desktop freeze). Green (≥25 GB) → a render may proceed. Source: services/render_vram.py + the media_infra_health VRAM preflight (#2394). Video staying quiet during active desktop use is EXPECTED here until the VRAM-reclaim + idle-WSL-reset follow-up lands. If you retune pipeline_gpu_index, update the gpu filter in this query.

panels.title: Gaming Detection & Pipeline Status
panels.description: Shows when gaming pauses the pipeline vs active GPU usage

panels.title: VRAM headroom (dedicated)
panels.description: Per-GPU dedicated-VRAM headroom = (card total - 3 GB desktop reserve) - VRAM used, one series per GPU. Uses each card's real nvidia_gpu_memory_total_mib so it stays correct across a mixed-size multi-GPU rig (e.g. 32 GB 5090 + 24 GB 3090) instead of hardcoding the primary card's size. When a series trends toward the 0 line the NVIDIA driver is about to spill that card's VRAM into system RAM (the WDDM desktop freeze). The Windows shared-memory spill counter itself isn't in Prometheus yet (no host GPU-spill collector on Linux either) — a future exporter task.

panels.title: Wall Power (Shelly plug)
panels.description: True AC wall power metered at the outlet by the Shelly plug (psu_total_power_watts via the gpu-exporter's /rpc/Switch.GetStatus poll). Reboot-proof and independent of the PSU's USB HID — the permanent wall-power source (see docs/operations/wall-power-metering.md). Compare with the DC-output stat beside it: wall − DC = PSU conversion loss.

panels.title: PSU DC Output — total (HX1500i)

targets.expr: node_hwmon_power_watt{chip=~".*1b1c.*"} * on(chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{label="power total"}

panels.description: Total DC output power from the corsair-psu kernel driver via node_exporter hwmon. Pairs with the Shelly wall stat: wall − DC = conversion loss. (The driver's own input-power estimate reads garbage, hence the plug.)

panels.title: Mains Voltage (Shelly, AC in)
panels.description: True outlet voltage from the Shelly wall-plug meter — not a PSU-internal estimate. Dashed lines mirror the MainsVoltageLow / MainsVoltageCritical alert bands at 92% / 87% of a 120V nominal (110.4V / 104.4V). Those alert thresholds live in app_settings (prometheus.threshold.psu_nominal_line_voltage_volts and the two percent keys); if you retune them there, update these lines to match. Sustained undervoltage ends in an uncommanded hard power-off that leaves no journal entry — see docs/operations/wall-power-metering.md.

panels.title: Power Over Time

targets.expr: node_hwmon_power_watt{chip=~".*1b1c.*"} * on(chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{label="power total"}

panels.description: Wall power (Shelly outlet meter) vs PSU DC output (corsairpsu kernel driver) over time — the gap is PSU conversion loss. +12V rail carries the GPU load.

targets.rawSql: SELECT created_at AS time, (cost_usd / NULLIF(duration_ms, 0) * 3600000.0 * 24)::float AS "Est. Daily Cost" FROM cost_logs WHERE cost_type LIKE 'electricity%' AND $__timeFilter(created_at) ORDER BY created_at

panels.title: PSU Temperatures
panels.description: HX1500i VRM + case temperature from the corsair-psu kernel driver via node_exporter (replaced the iCUE CSV export at the Pop!_OS migration).

panels.title: UPS status
panels.description: ON BATTERY = the transfer relay has left line power (ups.status flag OB from the host's upsd via the nut-exporter container). Text + color together by design (colorblind-safe). Mirrors the UpsOnBattery page (critical → Telegram after 1m on battery). An off/bypassed UPS also reads ON LINE here — the status-flag timeline at the bottom of this row carries the full truth.

panels.title: Battery charge
panels.description: battery.charge from the UPS. The driver forces a clean shutdown at its own floor (battery.charge.low — overlaid live on the charge history panel below), and UpsLowBattery pages at prometheus.threshold.ups_battery_charge_critical_percent (default 50%) — but only while actually discharging, so a post-outage recharge never pages.

panels.title: Runtime remaining
panels.description: battery.runtime — the UPS's own runtime estimate at the CURRENT load. It recalculates as load changes (a GPU burst can halve it between scrapes) and CyberPower firmware clamps it near the shutdown floor, so read it as an order of magnitude, not a promise. NUT forces the clean shutdown at battery.runtime.low.

panels.title: UPS load
panels.description: ups.load as percent of the inverter's own rating (ups.realpower.nominal — 1000W on the operator unit). UpsLoadHigh warns on a sustained 85-95% band; UpsLoadCritical pages at ≥95% — calibrated on the 2026-07-31 overload trip (GPU burst transients on a >90% standing load, during a sag transfer). Tune via prometheus.threshold.ups_load_warning_percent / ups_load_critical_percent.

panels.title: Est. draw on UPS
panels.description: load% × the unit's rated watts (network_ups_tools_ups_realpower_nominal) = estimated true draw on the battery-backed outlets. This is the number to hold against the inverter rating when deciding what lives on the protected bank vs the surge-only bank — in the 2026-07-31 trip the PC alone burst past its 1000W rating mid-transfer.

panels.title: UPS input vs output voltage
panels.description: What the UPS measures at its input (orange) vs what it delivers to the PC (blue, output.voltage) — the lines separate exactly when the AVR is correcting (BOOST/TRIM lanes in the timeline below). Y pinned to 90-130V for a 120V service so chronic sag is visible at a glance; the dashed 114V line mirrors UpsInputVoltageLow (prometheus.threshold.ups_input_voltage_low_volts — 114V = ANSI C84.1 Range A lower bound; retune both together). The operator house ran 93-114V for days in 2026-07. Independent second meter alongside the Shelly's Mains Voltage panel above (MainsVoltage* alerts) — two taps on the same story.

panels.title: UPS load (% of inverter rating)
panels.description: ups.load history. Dashed lines mirror the UpsLoadHigh / UpsLoadCritical bands (prometheus.threshold.ups_load_warning_percent / ups_load_critical_percent, default 85/95%); y tops at 110% because overload excursions read past 100 (OVER lane in the timeline below). The 2026-07-31 trip: the PC alone — GPU burst transients stacked on a >90% standing load — on a 1000W unit, during a sag transfer.

panels.title: Battery charge
panels.description: battery.charge with the driver's OWN floors overlaid live: battery.charge.low is the forced-clean-shutdown line (30% on the operator rig — set via override.* in /etc/nut/ups.conf; retune NUT and this line moves with it), battery.charge.warning the firmware's warning level. The dashed 50% threshold mirrors the UpsLowBattery page floor (prometheus.threshold.ups_battery_charge_critical_percent), which only fires while discharging.

panels.title: Battery runtime remaining
panels.description: battery.runtime with battery.runtime.low overlaid — NUT orders the clean shutdown when runtime crosses that floor (300s on the operator rig). The estimate recalculates with load, so expect step changes when GPU work starts or stops; a runtime that steps DOWN while on battery is the pack telling you the truth early.

panels.title: Battery voltage
panels.description: battery.voltage vs nominal — pack health at a glance. A float voltage parked well above nominal is healthy (27.2V on a 24V PbAcid pack); a reading sagging toward nominal AT REST is an aging pack that will under-deliver runtime when it finally matters. Always-on UPS packs typically want replacing every 3-5 years.

panels.title: UPS status flags
panels.description: ups.status decomposed into one lane per flag, lit only while active. OB = on battery, LB = low battery, OVER = overload (the 2026-07-31 trip signature), BOOST/TRIM = the AVR actively correcting under-/over-voltage (the audible relay clicks during sags — these lanes lighting up is the supply degrading BEFORE any transfer), CHRG/DISCHRG = battery direction, FSD = forced shutdown ordered, BYPASS = power flowing unprotected. Reconstructs an incident after the fact: sag → BOOST → OB → OVER reads left to right.

targets.rawSql: SELECT to_char("timestamp",'HH24:MI') as sample_time, utilization as util, temperature as temp, ROUND(power_draw::numeric) as watts, memory_used as vram, fan_speed as fan, clock_graphics as clock FROM gpu_metrics WHERE $__timeFilter("timestamp") ORDER BY "timestamp" DESC LIMIT 20

SELECT date_trunc('day',"timestamp")::date as day, ROUND(AVG(utilization)::numeric,1) as util, ROUND(AVG(temperature)::numeric,1) as temp, ROUND(AVG(power_draw)::numeric) as watts, COUNT(*) as samples FROM gpu_metrics WHERE $__timeFilter("timestamp") GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC

panels.title: Temperatures (hwmon)
panels.description: All labeled hwmon temperature sensors via node_exporter — k10temp (CPU Tctl/Tccd), asusec (board/VRM), corsairpsu (PSU VRM/case), nvme, amdgpu. Replaced the Windows-only AIDA64 shared-memory source (Pop!_OS migration).

panels.title: Fans (hwmon)
panels.description: All hwmon fan tachometers via node_exporter (PSU fan from corsairpsu, board fans from asusec). Replaced the iCUE CSV export (Pop!_OS migration).

panels.title: Component Power — live (hwmon)
panels.description: PSU rail power (corsairpsu: total/+12V/+5V/+3.3V) + AMD PPT via node_exporter hwmon. GPU board power lives on the VRAM/Power panels (nvidia_gpu_*). Replaced AIDA64 CPU-Package/GPU1 (Pop!_OS migration).

panels.title: Voltages (hwmon)
panels.description: Labeled hwmon voltages via node_exporter — corsairpsu v_out rails (+12V/+5V/+3.3V) and board sensors. Replaced the AIDA64 source (Pop!_OS migration).

panels.title: Available RAM
panels.description: node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes = truly-free + reclaimable memory. When this trends toward 0 the desktop compositor starves and the UI freezes. The PoindexterHostMemoryLow warning fires under 4 GB sustained.

panels.title: Commit vs RAM
panels.description: node_memory_Committed_AS_bytes / node_memory_CommitLimit_bytes. Over 100% means committed memory exceeds physical RAM — the host is leaning on swap. Sustained high commit is the structural oversubscription behind the freezes.

panels.title: Page-out rate
panels.description: rate(node_vmstat_pswpout[5m]) — pages/s swapped out (memory-pressure eviction, not ordinary file I/O). The PoindexterHostMemoryThrashing critical fires over 2000/s — the freeze-in-progress signal.

panels.title: Available RAM (headroom)
panels.description: Host available RAM over time. The line at 4 GB is the PoindexterHostMemoryLow warning floor; when this approaches 0 the desktop compositor stalls (the host-memory freeze).

panels.title: Swap write rate (thrash)
panels.description: rate(node_vmstat_pswpout[5m]) — sustained swap page-outs = memory-pressure eviction. The line at 2000 pages/s is the PoindexterHostMemoryThrashing critical floor; spikes here are freeze-in-progress episodes.

panels.title: Pipeline pause for gaming
panels.description: Seconds the pipeline surrendered the GPU because a game was detected. gap-fill (poindexter#855): live Prometheus metric that was on no dashboard
CHARTER: live GPU-lock wait-queue depth (gpu_queue mirror rows). >0 sustained = the scheduler is arbitrating contention; pair with the wait-p90 table to judge whether waits are healthy.
panels.title: GPU queue depth (now)

panels.description: CHARTER: rolling GPU-lock hold durations per (owner, phase) from gpu_lease_stats — the same p50/p90 the P1 admission ETA uses. Sanity-check p90 against known render/writer durations during the soak.

targets.rawSql: SELECT owner, phase, samples, round(ewma_ms::numeric) AS ewma_ms, round(p50_ms::numeric) AS p50_ms, round(p90_ms::numeric) AS p90_ms, updated_at FROM gpu_lease_stats ORDER BY p90_ms DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 20

panels.title: GPU hold durations — p50/p90 by owner·phase

description: CHARTER: GPU/PSU/wall power + host-memory pressure — thermal, electrical, and RAM headroom and electricity cost. GPU live is single-sourced from Prometheus nvidia_gpu_* (#653); the gpu_metrics SQL tables here are history only. Host-memory row added 2026-07-10 (desktop-freeze investigation).
